==English== ===Alternative forms=== * {{alt|en|licence||noun|Commonwealth}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈlaɪ.səns/}} * {{audio|en|en-us-license.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|aɪsəns|s=2}} * {{hyph|en|li|cense}} ===Etymology 1=== {{wp}} From {{inh|en|enm|licence}}, {{m|enm|licens}}, {{m|enm|lisence}}, {{m|enm|lissens}}, {{m|enm|licance}}, from {{der|en|fro|licence}}, from {{der|en|la|licentia||license}}, from {{m|la|licens}}, present participle of {{m|la|licere||to be allowed, be allowable}}; compare {{m|la|linquere}}, {{cog|grc|λείπω||leave}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun|~}} {{tlb|en|American spelling}} # A [[legal]] [[document]] giving [[official]] [[permission]] to do something; a [[permit]]. # The legal [[term]]s under which a person is [[allow]]ed to use a product, especially [[software]]. # [[freedom|Freedom]] to [[deviate]] deliberately from normally applicable [[rule]]s or [[practice]]s (especially in [[behaviour]] or [[speech]]). #* {{quote-book|en|year=2012|author=Chris Seepe|title=The Conspiracy to Assassinate Jesus Christ|url=https://www.worldcat.org/title/conspiracy-to-assassinate-jesus-christ/oclc/885339746|page=5|text=In some instances, the author took '''license''' to include events which never happened, or to purposely create events which may run in the face of popular conjecture if the author felt it would help the story along.}} # [[excessive|Excessive]] freedom; [[lack]] of [[due]] [[restraint]]. #* {{RQ:Tennyson In Memoriam|XXVII|44|I envy not the beast that takes
⁠His '''license''' in the field of time,
⁠Unfetter’d by the sense of crime,
To whom a conscience never wakes; {{...}}}} # {{ellipsis of|en|driver's license}}. #: {{ux|en|In order to enter the building, I need to show my '''license'''.}} =====Usage notes===== * In British English, Canadian English, Australian English, Irish English, South African English and New Zealand English the noun is spelt {{m|en||licence}} and the verb is {{m|en||license}}. * The spelling {{m|en||licence}} is not used for either part of speech in the United States. =====Derived terms===== {{col|en|colicense|dramatic license |artistic license|license fee|license laundering |bare license English {{m|en|licentiate}}). ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # To [[authorize]] officially. #: {{ux|en|I am '''licensed''' to practice law in this state.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} {{ng|(applied to a piece of [[intellectual property]])}} ## To give formal [[authorization]] to use. ##: {{ux|en|It was decided to '''license''' Wikipedia under the GFDL.}} ##* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-22|volume=407|issue=8841|page=68 |title=[http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21579860-g8-pledges-tackle-three-ts-t-time T time] |passage=The ability to shift profits to low-tax countries by locating intellectual property in them, which is then '''licensed''' to related businesses in high-tax countries, is often assumed to be the preserve of high-tech companies.}} ## To acquire authorization to use, usually in exchange for [[compensation]]. ##: {{ux|en|The filmmakers '''licensed''' several iconic 80's songs for the soundtrack.}} ##* {{quote-journal|en|year=2000|journal=International Journal of Micrographics & Optical Technology |url=https://books.google.ca/books?id=nugOAQAAMAAJ&q=%22licensed+the+image%22 |text=As part of the strategic relationship, Microsoft has '''licensed''' the image segmentation, compression and viewing technology from ScanSoft. }} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=2007|author=Steve Swayne|title=How Sondheim Found His Sound |url=https://books.google.ca/books?id=X7HWzVOvtEwC&pg=PP216&dq=%22licensed+the+song%22 |text=They changed their campaign, '''licensed''' the song and used it for over six years in all of their advertising. }} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To give [[permission]] or [[freedom]] to; [[accept]]. #* {{RQ:Dickens Little Dorrit|passage=Intruders there were in Harley Street, of whom it was not aware; but Mr and Mrs Merdle it delighted to honour. Society was aware of Mr and Mrs Merdle. Society had said ‘Let us '''license''' them; let us know them.’}} # {{lb|en|linguistics|transitive}} To [[permit]] (as [[grammatically]] correct). #: {{ux|en|No English adverbs have mandatory complements, and most don't even '''license''' optional ones.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2014|author=Hagit Borer|title=Parametric Syntax: Case Studies in Semitic and Romance Languages |url=https://books.google.ca/books?id=MUZbDAAAQBAJ&pg=PA28 |text=Kayne argues that the crucial fact which '''licenses''' preposition stranding in English but not in French is the fact that in English verbs and prepositions assign Case similarly, and hence they govern similarly. }} =====Derived terms===== {{col3|en |licensable |licensee |licenser |licensor|licensability |crosslicense |delicense |relicense |sublicense |unlicense}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|to authorize officially}} * Bulgarian: * Dutch: * Finnish: * German: * Greek: * Hungarian: * Māori: * Spanish: * Swedish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to give formal authorization to use}} * Bulgarian: * Dutch: * Finnish: * German: * Hungarian: * Māori: * Spanish: * Swedish: * Welsh: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to acquire authorization to use}} * Bulgarian: * Spanish: {{trans-bottom}} ===References=== {{reflist}} ===Further reading=== * {{R:Webster 1913}} * {{R:Century}} * {{R:Britannica 1911|Licence}} ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=ceeilns|selenic|silence}}
